record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For the Cauchy problem for the KPZ equation, can one prove strong 3:2:1 KPZ universality for a wide class of initial data and identify the limiting process predicted by physics?

evidence.quote: The most challenging open problem regarding the KPZ equation is to prove 3 : 2 : 1 KPZ universality in the strong sense of Corwin, Quastel and Remenik [30] alluded to above, for solutions of the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation for a wide set of initial data, and to identify the limiting process.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation on the real line,
   ∂_t h(t,x) = (1/2) ∂_x^2 h(t,x) + (1/2)(∂_x h(t,x))^2 + ξ(t,x),  t > 0, x ∈ ℝ,
where ξ is space–time white noise, with the Cauchy (initial value) problem h(0,x) = h_0(x), interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transformation h = log Z, where Z solves the multiplicative stochastic heat equation ∂_t Z = (1/2) ∂_x^2 Z + Z ξ with initial data Z(0,x) = e^{h_0(x)}.

For ε > 0 define the rescaled height function
   h_ε(t,x) := ε^{1/2}( h(ε^{-3/2} t, ε^{-1} x) + (1/24) ε^{-3/2} t ),
reflecting the conjectural 1:2:3 (equivalently 3:2:1) KPZ scaling.

Let 𝔥(t,x;𝔥_0) denote the KPZ fixed point, the Markov process on upper semicontinuous functions constructed as a scaling limit of TASEP with initial profile 𝔥_0.

Problem. Determine the largest natural class 𝒞 of (random or deterministic) initial data h_0 — including the standard physically relevant cases such as flat, narrow-wedge (delta), stationary (two-sided Brownian), and general initial profiles in 𝒞 — for which, with appropriate ε-dependent rescaling h_0 ↦ 𝔥_0^ε of the initial conditions converging to 𝔥_0, the rescaled height functions h_ε converge in distribution (in a suitable topology of upper semicontinuous functions) to the KPZ fixed point started from 𝔥_0:
   h_ε(·,·) ⟹ 𝔥(·,·;𝔥_0)  as ε ↓ 0.
That is, prove strong 3:2:1 KPZ universality for the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation for a wide class of initial data, and identify the limiting space–time process.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Quastel and Sarkar (arXiv:2008.06584, published 2023) and independently Virág proved convergence of the KPZ equation under 1:2:3 scaling to the KPZ fixed point for a broad class of initial data, including the four classical cases. Subsequent work (Wu and others) extended convergence to the directed landscape. Whether this constitutes the fullest version of "strong" KPZ universality for all physically natural initial data remains an active area, but the core convergence result has been established.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of exclusion processes and the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point
status_evidence.snippet: Under the 1:2:3 scaling, the height function of finite range asymmetric exclusion processes and the KPZ equation converge to the KPZ fixed point.
status_evidence.claim: Quastel and Sarkar proved convergence of the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point under 1:2:3 scaling.

status_evidence.title: The KPZ equation and the directed landscape
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence of the KPZ equation, with general initial data, to the directed landscape.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to convergence to the directed landscape have appeared.

status_evidence.title: KPZ fixed point - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The KPZ fixed point is conjectured to be the universal limit of a wide range of stochastic models in the KPZ universality class.
status_evidence.claim: Universality across the full class remains a guiding conjecture.
